bibliographic.title: Guidance for researchers and peer‑reviewers on the ethical use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in scientific research workflows
bibliographic.citation_apa: Watkins, R. (2023). Guidance for researchers and peer-reviewers on the ethical use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in scientific research workflows. AI and Ethics, 4, 969–974. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43681-023-00294-5

methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models (LLMs) used in scientific research workflows; examples include OpenAI ChatGPT and Google LaMDA

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is an opinion paper advocating norms, conventions, and standards for ethical LLM use by researchers and peer-reviewers in scientific research workflows. It addresses AI ethics and governance framing for LLMs but does not examine conversational governance, conversational AI systems, or LLM deployment in regulated operational environments central to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter/page 1 text was provided; metadata incorrectly labels the item as preprint though the source identifies it as a peer-reviewed journal opinion paper.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on limited excerpt. As an editorial opinion paper, it does not report empirical sampling, data collection, or analysis; it argues for developing ethical norms and standards for LLM use in research practice.

cerqual.explanation: The provided text coherently argues for ethical norms for LLM use in scientific research, but evidence is conceptual and the excerpt is incomplete. Relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is indirect and limited.

coding.theme: Ethical governance of LLM use in scientific research
coding.subtheme: Norms and standards for researchers and peer-reviewers

synthesis.main_claim: Researchers and peer-reviewers currently lack guidance on ethical LLM use in scientific research, and norms, conventions, and standards should be developed by applying AI ethics principles.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an editorial call to establish ethical norms and standards for LLM use and reporting in scientific research workflows, including guidance needs for peer-reviewers.
synthesis.limitations: No empirical evaluation, operational governance mechanisms, conversational system design, or regulated-domain deployment analysis are presented in the provided text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on ethical norms and standards for LLM use; not central evidence for conversational governance in regulated operational environments.
